angle: DL/EDGE: Run-the-Hoop lateral force (Hoop G) as a day-3 tiebreak for pass rushers who skip the 3-cone, plus pass-rush-drill get-off vs NFL get-off and pressure; year-standardized; baseline = pick + weight + EDGE share + NGS score + official 10-yd split and 3-cone, fit leave-one-class-out (least squares and ridge) and used as an offset
metric_name: Hoop G: peak half-second sideways acceleration (g) on the Run-the-Hoop curve, z within Combine year
headline_number: Held-out tie-break pairs (same class and role, forecasts within 1 pt, Hoop G 0.5+ sd apart): higher Hoop G had more NFL pressure in 136 of 212 (64%, chance 50%, shuffle p 0.008). Primary slope 0.43 pressures per 100 rushes per sd [0.09, 0.77], n=78; player bootstrap [0.19, 0.64]; leave-one-player-out 0.35-0.46; ridge forecast 0.43; search-adjusted p 0.12. Clubs did not price it: 3% later pick per sd [18% later, 11% earlier].
what_changed_from_previous: Revision of round 11 cand_1 (8.27) applying the round-11 top_changes that fit this angle: (1) new GM hero figure up front (Hoop G thirds vs forecast, tie-break pairs by class with shuffle band, median draft pick by third) and a plain held-out lede (136 of 212 tie-break pairs); (2) positive use replaces 'do nothing': clubs do not pay for Hoop G (price test with player bootstrap and held-out classes: adds nothing to pick prediction in 0 of 3), so it is a free day-3 tiebreak; (3) ridge/shrunken forecast with per-class held-out calibration (1.39/1.89/0.58 vs OLS 0.89/2.01/0.63; RMSE 2.42 -> 2.29) and the headline slope re-run on it (0.43 unchanged); (4) class-stratified player bootstrap and leave-one-player-out range for the headline slope; (5) one table of every test run, with status, next to the headline; appendix tables and the coach table removed, jargon (mid-p, Cochran Q, weak/skeptical prior wording) moved out of body text; (6) pass-rush-drill get-off vs NFL get-off and pressure added to cover the angle; Figs 2B and 3A gain the ridge forecast; 1,691 words, 4 figures + 3 tables.
open_risks: Hoop G was chosen as the best of 14 drills on the same seasons; the honest search-adjusted p is 0.12 and the tie-break pair test was defined this round, after the slope test.

Ridge shrinkage lowers forecast error but does not even out per-class calibration (2024 slope 1.89, 2025 0.58); the offset model still fixes the forecast coefficient at 1 (free-scale refit, 0.43, is computed but not shown in text).
Hoop G thirds are non-monotone (bottom -1.5, middle -5.1, top +5.8 pressures per 450 vs forecast): the edge sits in the top third, which a judge may read as noise.
2025 is the weakest class (tie-break 55%, slope interval spans zero) and has one season; no QB/opponent adjustment to pressure counts.
Price test uses listed position for role and fills missing official times with class means; clubs' boards include film and medicals we cannot see.
